# Handpress

> Adds an in-place editor to a hand-written static site. A non-technical owner signs in with
> Google, clicks the page and types; saving writes the HTML files and commits them to git.
> No templating, no database, no build step.

Use it for: small hand-built sites (tens of pages), one or two editors, a design that matters.
Do not use it for: hundreds of pages, many simultaneous authors, drafts or approval workflow,
content already in a database or a framework's content collection.

## Install

```
npm i -D handpress
npx handpress install ./public                                # editor.js + admin.html
npx handpress keys "public/*.html" --global "header, footer"  # adds data-e keys; re-run after hand-editing HTML
```

Load the editor only for editors, in the site's own script:

```
if (/(?:^|;\s*)ed=1/.test(document.cookie)) {
  var s = document.createElement('script'); s.src = '/editor.js'; s.defer = true;
  document.head.appendChild(s);
}
```

Server: a Cloudflare Worker (src/worker.js), or PHP on ordinary shared hosting
(`npx handpress install ./public_html --php` installs php/api.php plus Apache templates; saves
are live immediately there), or any host implementing the six endpoints below.
Configure with vars GITHUB_REPO, GITHUB_BRANCH, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and an EDITOR object of
{pages, dataFiles, globalBlocks, uploadDir, forceVisible}; secrets GITHUB_TOKEN, SESSION_SECRET,
ADMIN_EMAILS. Sign-in needs a Google OAuth client with the site's origin as an authorised origin.

## API

- GET  /api/config        {pages, dataFiles, globalBlocks, uploadDir, forceVisible, clientId}
- POST /api/login         {credential} Google ID token -> session cookie + readable `ed=1` cookie
- POST /api/logout
- GET  /api/me            {email} or 401
- GET  /api/file?path=    {path, content, sha}; refuses anything off the allowlist
- POST /api/save          {files:[{path, content|base64, sha}], message}; all files or none

## Keys

data-e="t12" text block · "m12" image · "i12" list item · data-e-list repeating container ·
a "g" prefix (gt12) means the element is inside a global block shared by every page.

## Design notes

The editor keeps two DOMs: the live page, and the page's source fetched from the server. Edits
apply to both, and only the source is saved, so a site's own JavaScript (rendered lists,
animated counters) never gets written into the files. Keys are how the two are matched.

Per-site quirks go in window.EDITOR_HOOKS: beforeEdit(el) to detach an element the site
animates, syncUnit(sourceEl, liveEl) to keep an attribute in step with edited text.
